english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep, our hearts pain us when we see this: a man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself. And the sheep has no wool."

english: Herdsman, someone stole three oxen! How shall I find them? A wise boy stole the cows of the gods. He bound bark on their feet, and they were seeking them. Did they seize the boy? They seized him; he sang them a song, and they laughed. Then I shall look for bark on the path! Seek, and take a spear!

english: Mother, who freed the dawn? An ill-minded one was hiding the cows and the dawn in a stone. Was there night then? There was night, and people wept. Then a god came, and he split the stone with a song. Did they come out? They came out, and the dawn grew bright. Will the dawn come in the morning? She comes in the morning. Now sleep, child!

english: Father, why do you look at the sheep in the evening? A wolf clothed itself in a sheep's wool. In the evening it went in among the sheep. Did the herdsman not see it? He did not see it, and at night it swallowed a sheep. How did he seize it? He caught sight of teeth under the wool, and he struck it down. So you look at the teeth of the sheep! I look at their teeth, and I do not see wolves.

english: Herdsman, why does the wolf go hungry? Hear a story! A hungry wolf met a dog. The dog said: 'Come with me to the house!' Did he go? He went, and he caught sight of the dog bound at the door. Did he stay? He did not stay. A free wolf is better than a bound dog. May I be free!

english: Father, the sky is rumbling! Why is it rumbling? Perkʷunos is pursuing the serpent. The serpent stole the cattle of Perkʷunos, and it hid under an oak. Will Perkʷunos find it? She was not dead: she was deceiving the men! The men threw her into the wagon, and she threw the fish down onto the path. And then she devoured them! She devoured them all, and the hungry men returned home.

english: Dear one, tell me a story about the bear, and I will sleep. A bear found honey in a tree. When he was sleeping, a fox ate all the honey. Did the bear not wake up? He did not wake up. Then she smeared honey on his mouth. When he woke up, she said: 'You ate up the honey!' And he believed her? He believed her. Bears are not wise.

english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep, our hearts pain us when we see this: a man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself. And the sheep has no wool."

english: Chief, does a horse speak? They do not speak; the horse of a hero said a word. Which word did it say? It said: 'Master, on this day you will die in battle.' Did the hero go into the battle? He went, and he did not tremble before death. Did it weep? It wept, and the hero died.

It did not stand up in the morning, and people were freezing. Did the herdsman give it back? He let it go, and it stood up again.

english: Old man, who is eating the sun? A great wolf is swallowing it; do not tremble, child. Will it vanish? Hear the story! The wolf swallowed the sun, and there was night. A hero struck it with a spear, and the sun came forth from its mouth. Where is the hero now? He is in the sky with the immortals. Look! It is coming back!

Then I shall not swim there; I shall swim in the river.

english: Old man, tell me a story! Did you drive off the enemies' cattle? I drove them off, young man. Ten men went out at night. Did you not grow afraid? My heart trembled. Then we found the cows in a field. Did the herdsmen see you? A boy saw us, and they were sleeping. Then we drove a hundred cows to the village. What did the king give you? He gave me a bull and great fame.

And from the twin's eyes? From his eyes he made the sun and the moon.

english: Of-Divine-Race, tell me the story of the serpent! Did it have three heads? It had three heads, and it stole the cows of the people. Who fought against it? The third son of a king fought against it. He cut off its three heads, and they came forth. Did he drive them to his own house? He gave them back to the people. So his fame is great. I want great fame!

english: Of-Goodly-Fame, tell me a sad story! A hero left his wife and his son, and he went to the fight. In a battle he met a young warrior. Was it his son? He was his son; the two men did not know it. Did they fight? They fought, and the father struck him down. I do not want that end! You asked for a sad story. In the morning I shall tell you something glad.

pie: ph₂ter wĺ̥kʷos h₂egʰós? solh₂wós wĺ̥kʷos ne h₂egʰós. wl̥kʷih₂és spélom h₂wisdʰí. wiḱpótis dwóh₁ swóh₁ suHnúh₁ déh₂newi léykʷt. déh₂nu tóh₁ h₁r̥h₁pyét? tóh₁ ne h₁r̥h₁pyét. wl̥kʷíh₂s tóh₁ réh₁tt tóybʰos-kʷe swóm h₂mélǵos déh₃t. h₂ukstā́m? h₂ukstā́m méǵh₂m̥-kʷe ḱóymom démetām. wl̥kʷíh₂s h₁uséwih₂.
english: Father, is the wolf evil? Not every wolf is evil. Hear the story of the she-wolf. A chief left his two sons by the river. Did the river carry them off? It did not carry them off. A she-wolf found them and gave them her milk. Did they grow up? They grew up, and they built a great village. The she-wolf is good!

pie: kʷíd nos ǵń̥h₃re h₁énosyo ḱóymosyo woyḱṓs h₃eh₃dḗr? dwóh₁ bʰréh₂terh₁e swósyo ph₂trés gʷṓs bʰéh₂getām. sényōs h₁wésyosm̥ bʰoh₂góm h₁áyto? h₁ím h₁áyto h₁éteros-kʷe h₁ím gʷʰént. kʷoynéh₂m kʷinéwt? h₁íh₂m̥ ne kʷinéwt h₁énom ḱóymom bʰéwgt. nu nos kʷoynéh₂m éti dʰl̥gʰónti. h₁íh₂m̥ dʰl̥gʰónti tṓys ḱóm bʰéh₂omes mē-kʷe wikṓmes.
english: Wise one, why do the dwellers of that village hate us? Two brothers were dividing their father's cattle. Did the older one take the better share? He took it, and the other struck him down. Did he pay the blood-price? He did not pay it; he fled to that village. Then they still owe us the blood-price! They owe it; let us speak with them, and let us not fight.

pie: méh₂ter moy bʰréh₂tēr mḗms sléh₂gʷt. spélom ḱléwse. wĺ̥kʷos h₂ŕ̥tḱons-kʷe mḗms widétām wikétām-kʷe. h₂wĺ̥pis sékʷt mḗms wos bʰéh₂gōh₂. h₁íh₂ h₁íd bʰéh₂get? tóybʰos h₃ésth₁h₂ déh₃t h₁íd-kʷe h₁ḗdt. nu moy bʰréh₂tr̥h₁ ḱóm ne wikṓh₂. h₁íd bʰéh₂getom h₂wĺ̥pis-kʷe h₁íd ne h₁édeti.
english: Mother, my brother took the meat! Listen to a story. A wolf and a bear found meat, and they fought. A fox said: 'Let me divide the meat for you two.' Did she divide it? She gave them the bones, and she ate it. Then I shall not fight with my brother. Divide it, you two, and no fox will eat it.
